questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following about the Western Ghats:
1. They are older than the Himalayas
2. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site
3. The Kasturirangan Committee recommended Ecologically Sensitive Areas (ESA) in Western Ghats
4. They receive more rainfall on the eastern slopes
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG - Western Ghats receive more rainfall on WESTERN slopes (windward side facing Arabian Sea monsoon). Eastern slopes are rain shadow (leeward). Western Ghats are ~150 million years old (older than Himalayas ~50 MY). UNESCO site since 2012. Kasturirangan (2013) was a compromise after Gadgil Committee's stricter recommendations.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following rivers originate from the Western Ghats?
1. Godavari
2. Krishna
3. Kaveri
4. Narmada
5. Tungabhadra
questions.explanation: All except Narmada. Godavari (Trimbakeshwar, Nashik), Krishna (Mahabaleshwar), Kaveri (Talakaveri, Brahmagiri Hills, Coorg), Tungabhadra (formed by Tunga+Bhadra in Karnataka) all originate in Western Ghats. Narmada originates from AMARKANTAK in Maikal Hills (Vindhya-Satpura region), NOT Western Ghats.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs:
Industrial Region - Key Industry
1. Hooghly - Jute
2. Mumbai-Pune - Cotton textiles
3. Chotanagpur - Iron and Steel
4. Bengaluru - Petrochemicals
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG - Bengaluru is famous for IT/electronics/aerospace, NOT petrochemicals. Petrochemical hubs are Jamnagar (Gujarat - world's largest refinery), Haldia (WB), Mangalore (Karnataka). Hooghly belt has ~60% of India's jute mills. Mumbai-Pune is India's oldest cotton textile region. Chotanagpur has Jamshedpur (TISCO), Bokaro, Rourkela steel plants.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
The 'Rain Shadow' region in India includes:
1. Western Rajasthan
2. Eastern slopes of Western Ghats in Karnataka
3. Leeward side of Aravalli Hills
4. Ladakh
questions.explanation: All are rain shadow areas. Western Rajasthan: Aravallis block moisture (Thar Desert). Eastern Western Ghats: Karnataka Plateau receives less rain (Deccan leeward). Aravalli leeward: western Rajasthan gets minimal monsoon. Ladakh: behind multiple Himalayan ranges, extremely dry (<10cm rainfall). Rain shadow = area on leeward side of mountains receiving significantly less precipitation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's nuclear power plants and their locations:
1. Kudankulam - Tamil Nadu (coastline)
2. Tarapur - Maharashtra (coastline)
3. Narora - Uttar Pradesh (inland, on Ganga)
4. Kaiga - Karnataka (inland, in Western Ghats)
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correctly located. Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu, coast - VVER reactors). Tarapur (Maharashtra, coast - India's first nuclear plant, 1969). Narora (UP, on Ganga - PHWR). Kaiga (Karnataka, in Western Ghats forest area near Kali river - PHWR). Other plants: Rawatbhata (Rajasthan), Kakrapar (Gujarat), Kalpakkam (Tamil Nadu - PFBR).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following states does the Narmada river NOT flow through?
questions.explanation: Narmada does NOT flow through Rajasthan. It flows through: Madhya Pradesh (originates Amarkantak, flows most of its course ~1,077 km in MP), Maharashtra (brief stretch through northern Maharashtra ~74 km), and Gujarat (enters via Bharuch and empties into Gulf of Khambhat ~160 km). Total length: 1,312 km.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following about Indian islands:
1. Andaman Islands are separated from Nicobar Islands by the Ten Degree Channel
2. Lakshadweep islands are formed by coral deposits on submarine volcanic ridge
3. Pamban Island is connected to mainland by a bridge
4. Sriharikota is an island in Pulicat Lake
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. Ten Degree Channel (10°N latitude) separates Andaman (north) from Nicobar (south). Lakshadweep: coral atolls on a submarine ridge. Pamban Island (between India mainland and Sri Lanka) connected by Pamban Bridge (India's first sea bridge, opened 1914). Sriharikota (ISRO's launch center) is a barrier island between Pulicat Lake and Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
With reference to Indian monsoon, 'Break Monsoon' means:
1. Complete cessation of rainfall over entire India
2. Northward shift of the monsoon trough to the Himalayan foothills
3. Increased rainfall in the northeastern states during this period
4. It typically lasts for one week or more
questions.explanation: 2, 3, 4 correct. Statement 1 WRONG - Break monsoon does NOT mean complete cessation over entire India. It means the monsoon trough shifts northward to foothills, causing: REDUCED rainfall over most of India (plains) BUT INCREASED rainfall in NE India and Himalayan foothills. The break can last 1-3 weeks. This is different from monsoon withdrawal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following multipurpose river valley projects:
1. Bhakra-Nangal - Sutlej river
2. Hirakud - Mahanadi river
3. Nagarjuna Sagar - Godavari river
4. Tehri Dam - Bhagirathi river
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 WRONG - Nagarjuna Sagar is on KRISHNA river (Telangana-AP border), NOT Godavari. Bhakra-Nangal (Sutlej, HP-Punjab border, India's highest gravity dam). Hirakud (Mahanadi, Odisha, world's longest earthen dam). Tehri (Bhagirathi, Uttarakhand, India's highest dam at 260m). Godavari projects include Polavaram (AP).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the Deccan Plateau is/are correct?
1. It is triangular in shape, bordered by Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, and Satpura range
2. It slopes from west to east
3. Most rivers flow eastward
4. The Malwa Plateau is part of the Deccan Plateau
questions.explanation: All correct. Deccan Plateau: triangular, bounded by Western Ghats (west), Eastern Ghats (east), Satpura/Vindhya (north). General slope west→east (hence most rivers flow east into Bay of Bengal). Narmada/Tapi are exceptions (flow west through rift valleys). Malwa Plateau (MP) is considered part of the broader Deccan/Central Highlands system.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's natural vegetation zones:
1. Tropical Evergreen forests are found in areas with >200cm rainfall
2. Tropical Deciduous forests are the most widespread in India
3. Mangrove forests are found in the Sundarbans and Andaman-Nicobar
4. Alpine vegetation is found above 3,600m in the Himalayas
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. Evergreen (Western Ghats, NE India, A&N - >200cm rain, no dry season). Deciduous forests (Monsoon forests) cover largest area of India - shed leaves in dry season. Mangroves in tidal areas: Sundarbans (largest), Bhitarkanika, Pichavaram, A&N. Alpine/Tundra vegetation above 3,600m: mosses, lichens, grasslands in higher Himalayas.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
With reference to India's coal reserves:
1. Jharkhand has the largest coal reserves in India
2. Gondwana coal accounts for about 98% of India's coal reserves
3. Tertiary coal is found in northeastern India
4. India is the world's largest importer of coking coal
questions.explanation: All correct. Jharkhand (~26% of India's reserves, Jharia coalfield is richest). Gondwana coal (Permian age, 250 MY): 98% of reserves, found in Damodar valley, Godavari, Mahanadi, Wardha basins. Tertiary coal (younger, 15-60 MY): Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal - lower quality. India imports ~85% of coking coal needs (for steel) mainly from Australia.
